children: Brand Leadership Showcase: Building India's Hospitality Legacy for the Next Century | Suma Venkatesh, Executive VP - Real Estate & Development, Indian Hotels Company Ltd (IHCL)

For more than a century, Indian Hotels Company (IHCL) has been closely associated with the evolution of organised hospitality in India. From the opening of The Taj Mahal Palace in Bombay in 1903, the company has expanded from a single iconic hotel into a multi-brand hospitality platform spanning luxury, upscale, full-service, midscale and experiential formats. Today, as India's hospitality market enters another phase of expansion, IHCL is looking at how that legacy can be extended through a wider portfolio, deeper geographic reach and a growing development pipeline.

That makes the perspective of Suma Venkatesh, Executive VP - Real Estate & Development, Indian Hotels Company Ltd (IHCL) particularly relevant to the owners, developers and investors attending the Indian Hospitality Summit & Awards 2026 at JW Marriott New Delhi Aerocity.
Building scale without losing the legacy

IHCL's growth today is not being built around Taj alone. Its expanded brandscape includes Taj, Claridges Collection, Brij, Atmantan, SeleQtions, Clarks, Gateway, Vivanta, Tree of Life and Ginger, alongside newer businesses and formats. In August 2026, IHCL reported that its portfolio had reached 645 hotels across more than 300 locations in 15 countries, with the company targeting a 700-hotel portfolio under its Accelerate 2030 strategy.

The development numbers show the scale of that expansion. By June 2026, IHCL had 382 operating hotels and 263 hotels in the pipeline, taking the total portfolio to 645. Taj accounted for 93 operating hotels and 57 pipeline hotels, while Ginger had 166 operating hotels and 96 pipeline hotels. These figures are global and distinguish properties already operating from those signed for future development.

The pace of development has continued. In the first quarter of FY2027, IHCL signed 20 hotels and opened 11. Seventeen of the 20 signings were across Gateway, Ginger and Tree of Life, with projects taking the brands into destinations including Bharatpur, Trichy, Sindhudurg, Jawai and Wayanad, as well as deeper penetration of established markets such as Mumbai, Goa, Agra and Kolkata.

For development partners, the significance lies in the range of markets being addressed. The expansion is not limited to India's largest metros. Recent signings include a 151-key Gateway in Raipur and a 111-key Ginger in Nava Raipur, while IHCL also signed a 125-key Gateway in Sambalpur, Odisha. The latter takes IHCL's Odisha presence to eight hotels, including three under development. These are signed projects, not operating hotels.
A portfolio designed for different markets

The expansion also reflects a deliberate use of different brands for different demand environments. Gateway is being developed as a full-service proposition, while Ginger is positioned in the midscale segment. Tree of Life addresses experiential leisure and amã Stays & Trails the premium homestay segment. This allows IHCL to pursue opportunities across business, leisure, pilgrimage, emerging urban centres and destination markets without relying on a single hotel format.

In August 2026, IHCL formalised this approach through the creation of a Select Service Business, bringing together Ginger, Tree of Life, amã Stays & Trails and Qmin. The vertical comprises 260 Ginger hotels, more than 40 Tree of Life resorts, more than 360 amã Stays & Trails bungalows and more than 100 Qmin outlets. Because these figures cover different formats and businesses, they should not be treated as a single hotel count.

IHCL has described the new vertical as a “non-linear growth engine”, targeting an enterprise revenue CAGR of more than 25 per cent under Accelerate 2030. That is a forward-looking company target, rather than an achieved growth rate.

The scale of the current expansion is underpinned by a longer-term strategy. IHCL's FY2025-26 results reported consolidated revenue of Rs 9,971 crore, up 16 per cent, with EBITDA reaching Rs 3,477 crore. The company said its multi-brand presence, diversification by brand, contract structure and geography had supported growth and resilience.

The company also invested more than Rs 1,000 crore during FY2026 across greenfield projects, hotel expansion, renovations and digital initiatives. Its development strategy has therefore involved both organic expansion and investment in existing assets and newer businesses. The next stage is set out in Accelerate 2030, under which IHCL aims to reach 700 hotels, double consolidated revenue to Rs 15,000 crore and deliver a 20 per cent ROCE.
